scenes.visual: Title card 'Spending ATP, Rebuilding ATP' fades in over a cartoon sandwich beside a cartoon leg. THE WORLD, kept for both films: 16:9, warm cream background, flat cartoon shapes, no molecular structures. COLOUR MAP, the same in every scene and in the second film: GLUCOSE = SAND-coloured block of six segments; ATP = GOLD round token with three small GOLD beads in a row; ADP = the same GOLD token with only two beads; loose PHOSPHATE = a single GOLD bead on its own; WATER = small PALE-AQUA drops; OXYGEN = BLUE dots; CARBON DIOXIDE = GREY puffs; MITOCHONDRION = OLIVE-GREEN bean with a wavy inner fold; HEAT = faint RED shimmer; LACTATE and ETHANOL (second film only) = ORANGE halves. COUNTER, top right, in both films: 'ATP rebuilt from this glucose: n'. Anything not computed is labelled 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: You just ate a sandwich, and your leg muscles are well stocked with sugar. So why can't a muscle simply burn that sugar to pull? The answer is a small molecule called A T P.
scenes.caption: You just ate a sandwich, and your leg muscles are well stocked with sugar. So why can't a muscle simply burn that sugar to pull? The answer is a small molecule called ATP.
scenes.visual: The sandwich shrinks into a stream of SAND glucose blocks that flows down into a cartoon leg. Zoom into one long muscle fibre packed with SAND blocks. The fibre tries to contract; a big question mark appears over the SAND blocks: 'burn the sugar directly?'. A single GOLD token with three beads rolls into view, labelled 'ATP'.
scenes.narration: You just ate a sandwich, and your leg muscles are well stocked with sugar. So why can't a muscle simply burn that sugar to pull? The answer is a small molecule called ATP.

scenes.tts: Every working cell spends energy. A muscle cell pulls. A nerve cell pumps charged particles across its membrane. Almost every cell builds proteins. None of these jobs runs on glucose directly. They run on A T P, a molecule that carries energy to the jobs that use it.
scenes.caption: Every working cell spends energy. A muscle cell pulls. A nerve cell pumps charged particles across its membrane. Almost every cell builds proteins. None of these jobs runs on glucose directly. They run on ATP, a molecule that carries energy to the jobs that use it.
scenes.visual: Three small panels slide in as each job is named: a muscle fibre shortening; a nerve cell with small plus-sign dots being pushed through its outline; a cell stringing beads into a chain labelled 'protein'. Each panel has a GOLD token feeding into it. A SAND glucose block tries to plug into each panel and bounces off, with a small red X. Label under all three: 'jobs run on ATP'.
scenes.narration: Every working cell spends energy. A muscle cell pulls. A nerve cell pumps charged particles across its membrane. Almost every cell builds proteins. None of these jobs runs on glucose directly. They run on ATP, a molecule that carries energy to the jobs that use it.

scenes.tts: A T P has three phosphate groups in a row. When it reacts with water, the end phosphate comes off. What is left is A D P, with only two. That reaction releases the energy the muscle uses to pull.
scenes.caption: ATP has three phosphate groups in a row. When it reacts with water, the end phosphate comes off. What is left is ADP, with only two. That reaction releases the energy the muscle uses to pull.
scenes.visual: Close-up of one GOLD token with three beads, the beads labelled 'phosphate groups'. A PALE-AQUA water drop touches it; the end bead pops off as a loose GOLD bead. The token, now with two beads, is relabelled 'ADP'. A small spark jumps from the reaction into the muscle fibre, which shortens. A word equation writes itself along the bottom: 'ATP + water → ADP + phosphate + energy for work'.
scenes.narration: ATP has three phosphate groups in a row. When it reacts with water, the end phosphate comes off. What is left is ADP, with only two. That reaction releases the energy the muscle uses to pull.

scenes.tts: Here's the catch. A cell keeps only a small supply of A T P. Watch that supply while the muscle keeps pulling, again and again.
scenes.caption: Here's the catch. A cell keeps only a small supply of ATP. Watch that supply while the muscle keeps pulling, again and again.
scenes.visual: A shallow tray inside the fibre holds a small pile of GOLD three-bead tokens, labelled 'a small supply of ATP (schematic)'. The fibre pulls rhythmically; with each pull one token drops a bead and joins a growing pile of two-bead ADP tokens on the other side. The ATP pile visibly shrinks while the narrator speaks.
scenes.narration: Here's the catch. A cell keeps only a small supply of ATP. Watch that supply while the muscle keeps pulling, again and again.

scenes.tts: Suppose nothing rebuilt A T P from A D P. What would happen to this supply, and to the pulling?
scenes.caption: Suppose nothing rebuilt ATP from ADP. What would happen to this supply, and to the pulling?
scenes.visual: The action freezes mid-pull. The ATP tray is nearly empty; the ADP pile is large. A question card appears: 'If nothing rebuilds ATP... the supply? the pulling?' A small pause icon pulses.
scenes.narration: Suppose nothing rebuilt ATP from ADP. What would happen to this supply, and to the pulling?

scenes.visual: Hold on the frozen frame and the question card. A thin timer bar runs across the bottom.

scenes.tts: The supply would soon run low, and the pulling would stop. So a working cell rebuilds A T P from A D P all the time. Putting the phosphate back takes energy. That energy comes from taking glucose apart.
scenes.caption: The supply would soon run low, and the pulling would stop. So a working cell rebuilds ATP from ADP all the time. Putting the phosphate back takes energy. That energy comes from taking glucose apart.
scenes.visual: Play resumes: the last GOLD token is used and the fibre stops pulling and freezes in place (it does not go slack), labelled 'no ATP: pulling stops (schematic)'. Rewind with a quick blur. Now a curved arrow carries ADP tokens back toward the tray; each one gets a GOLD bead clicked back on. A SAND glucose block appears at the start of the arrow with a label 'energy from taking glucose apart'. The COUNTER appears top right: 'ATP rebuilt from this glucose: 0'.
scenes.narration: The supply would soon run low, and the pulling would stop. So a working cell rebuilds ATP from ADP all the time. Putting the phosphate back takes energy. That energy comes from taking glucose apart.

scenes.tts: Glucose holds energy in the way its atoms are bonded. Taking it apart starts in the cytoplasm, the jelly-like inside of the cell. These first steps split glucose in two and rebuild a little A T P.
scenes.caption: Glucose holds energy in the way its atoms are bonded. Taking it apart starts in the cytoplasm, the jelly-like inside of the cell. These first steps split glucose in two and rebuild a little ATP.
scenes.visual: Pull back to a whole round cell. The cytoplasm, the open space inside, glows faintly and is labelled 'cytoplasm'. One SAND six-segment block drifts in and splits into two three-segment halves. A couple of ADP tokens nearby get their third bead back. The COUNTER ticks up by a little without pausing.
scenes.narration: Glucose holds energy in the way its atoms are bonded. Taking it apart starts in the cytoplasm, the jelly-like inside of the cell. These first steps split glucose in two and rebuild a little ATP.

scenes.tts: With oxygen, the two halves move into a mitochondrion. This organelle finishes the job, down to carbon dioxide and water. Most of the A T P is rebuilt here.
scenes.caption: With oxygen, the two halves move into a mitochondrion. This organelle finishes the job, down to carbon dioxide and water. Most of the ATP is rebuilt here.
scenes.visual: BLUE oxygen dots stream into the cell. The two SAND halves enter an OLIVE-GREEN bean with a wavy fold, labelled 'mitochondrion'. Inside, the halves break into small pieces; GREY carbon dioxide puffs and PALE-AQUA water drops leave the bean. A burst of ADP tokens around the bean gets beads clicked on, one after another.
scenes.narration: With oxygen, the two halves move into a mitochondrion. This organelle finishes the job, down to carbon dioxide and water. Most of the ATP is rebuilt here.

scenes.tts: Count what one glucose gave back. With oxygen, it rebuilds about thirty A T P. Some energy also leaves as heat. That is one reason you warm up when you exercise.
scenes.caption: Count what one glucose gave back. With oxygen, it rebuilds about thirty ATP. Some energy also leaves as heat. That is one reason you warm up when you exercise.
scenes.visual: The COUNTER climbs steadily and settles on 'ATP rebuilt from this glucose: about 30'. A RED shimmer rises off the mitochondrion and the cell, labelled 'heat'. A small inset shows a runner's cheeks turning pink.
scenes.narration: Count what one glucose gave back. With oxygen, it rebuilds about thirty ATP. Some energy also leaves as heat. That is one reason you warm up when you exercise.

scenes.tts: Now the loop closes. Work turns A T P into A D P. Respiration turns A D P back into A T P. Round and round, for as long as the cell is alive.
scenes.caption: Now the loop closes. Work turns ATP into ADP. Respiration turns ADP back into ATP. Round and round, for as long as the cell is alive.
scenes.visual: A circle of two curved arrows forms. Top arrow, from GOLD three-bead to two-bead token, labelled 'cell work (muscle pulls)'. Bottom arrow, from two-bead back to three-bead, labelled 'respiration (glucose taken apart)'. Tokens travel round the loop continuously, and the muscle fibre beats in time.
scenes.narration: Now the loop closes. Work turns ATP into ADP. Respiration turns ADP back into ATP. Round and round, for as long as the cell is alive.

scenes.tts: This whole process is cellular respiration. Glucose and oxygen go in. Carbon dioxide and water come out, with energy, much of it captured in A T P. A T P is not energy itself. It is a molecule that carries it.
scenes.caption: This whole process is cellular respiration. Glucose and oxygen go in. Carbon dioxide and water come out, with energy, much of it captured in ATP. ATP is not energy itself. It is a molecule that carries it.
scenes.visual: The pieces on screen slide into one line at the bottom: SAND block + BLUE dots → GREY puffs + PALE-AQUA drops + a wide arrow labelled 'released energy'. Part of that arrow bends down to drive ADP + loose GOLD bead → GOLD three-bead token; the rest leaves as a separate RED heat shimmer. No ATP token stands for energy itself. The words appear beneath: 'glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + energy (much of it captured in ATP)'. Title above: 'cellular respiration'. A GOLD token gets a tag: 'a molecule that carries energy'.
scenes.narration: This whole process is cellular respiration. Glucose and oxygen go in. Carbon dioxide and water come out, with energy, much of it captured in ATP. ATP is not energy itself. It is a molecule that carries it.

scenes.tts: But a sprinting leg can need A T P faster than oxygen-using respiration can rebuild it. Yeast sealed in bread dough gets almost no oxygen at all. What happens then? Switch the oxygen off in the simulation and find out.
scenes.caption: But a sprinting leg can need ATP faster than oxygen-using respiration can rebuild it. Yeast sealed in bread dough gets almost no oxygen at all. What happens then? Switch the oxygen off in the simulation and find out.
scenes.visual: Split screen: a sprinter's leg pumping hard with a GOLD token meter dipping, and a ball of dough wrapped tightly in plastic with a few cartoon yeast cells inside. A BLUE oxygen tap above both is shown half-turned, with a question mark. A small button labelled 'oxygen: off?' blinks but is not pressed.
scenes.narration: But a sprinting leg can need ATP faster than oxygen-using respiration can rebuild it. Yeast sealed in bread dough gets almost no oxygen at all. What happens then? Switch the oxygen off in the simulation and find out.

scenes.visual: End card with the logo hexagon character. Take-home line: 'Cells spend ATP, then rebuild it by taking glucose apart.'
